content:
**Cold-review local artifact is findings-only, overwritten per round, gitignored and scattered across worktrees**

**What**: Verified (2026-09-08) what the cold-review pipeline persists locally. The stage writes `openspec/reviews/pr-NNN/cold-review.md` tagged `brain-findings/1` (brain/scripts/review/lib/findings-artifact.mjs:47,:201). That file is the engine's RAW findings, deliberately without a `protocol: brain-review/...` line so it cannot corrupt rev counting. The verdict itself (rev, gates, controls, APPROVE/REVISE) is built by brain:review and lives ONLY on the forge as a PR comment.

**Why**: Maintainer assumed reviews were written per PR in openspec and a local daemon could read the round history. Partly true: the file exists, but run-cold-review-stage.mjs:294 REMOVES the previous artifact before every run, so only the latest round survives. PR #872's file holds `[]` (final APPROVE); rev 1's REVISE blocker is gone locally.

**Where**: `openspec/reviews/` is gitignored (.gitignore:135, rationale at :112-134 → ticket #414). Files are scattered per worktree: main checkout has pr-801..pr-866 (24 dirs), brain-issue-820 has pr-872, brain-issue-870 has pr-871 — the artifact lands in whichever cwd ran `brain:review`.

**Learned**: For a dashboard that wants review-round history, the forge comment timeline is the only durable source; the port has no PR-comment read verb (derive-review.mjs:11-26). A per-round local log (`rev-N`) could be appended at post time in poster.mjs since that is the one moment the machine holds the full verdict — but it would be a derived cache, never the record (ADR-0031 framing).
